definition: Yap Speech Cloud was a multimodal speech recognition system developed by American technology company Yap Inc.
details: It offered a fully cloud-based speech-to-text transcription platform that was used by customers such as Microsoft. The Company was a contestant at the inaugural TechCrunch conference and was subsequently acquired by Amazon in September 2011 to help develop products such as Alexa Voice Service, Echo, and Fire TV.

explainer.lead: Yap Inc. built Yap Speech Cloud, a fully cloud-based speech-to-text transcription platform used by customers such as Microsoft. It matters because Amazon acquired the company in 2011 to help develop products like Alexa Voice Service, Echo and Fire TV.

tiers.eli5: A company that built a cloud service for turning speech into text, which Amazon bought to help build its voice products.
tiers.practitioner: Its fully cloud-based speech-to-text transcription platform served customers including Microsoft; the team went to Amazon in September 2011 in support of Alexa Voice Service, Echo, and Fire TV.
tiers.paperLevel: Yap Speech Cloud was a multimodal speech recognition system developed by American technology company Yap Inc., offering a fully cloud-based speech-to-text transcription platform. The company was acquired by Amazon in September 2011.
